definition: A distributed training approach where the same model is replicated across multiple devices, each processing a different subset of the training data in parallel.
details: Data parallelism is one of the simplest and most common distributed training strategies, with gradients synchronized across devices after each step.
story: Picture a librarian organizing a million slips of paper so that any one of them can be found in a heartbeat. The examples a machine reads become the world it believes in. Better ingredients make a better meal, and the same is true here. Garbage in, garbage out — and the reverse: clean, representative data makes the model quietly brilliant. That care with the raw material is Data Parallelism.
